edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Welding fumes can deliver inhaled manganese and ultrafine particles to the nervous system, providing a plausible route to basal-ganglia toxicity and parkinsonian syndromes.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2026 Ryoo meta analysis in Am J Ind Med, which ties welding fume exposure to parkinson's disease in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
